create.title: Exact nonzero centering, selected-capacity correction, and Nyquist-fold cancellation
create.statement_tex: Fix A>0, q=4N, K=sqrt(NM), M^(3/4)(log(2X))^A<V<=K, and for every odd d|N put c=q/d and H=c/2. Let G_N(t)=1_(N|t)chi_4(t/N), A_j=Bhat_j(0), and retain the literal complex B_j with its real zero-extended profile, exact residual phase, asymmetric cell, signed blocks, transitions, and endpoints. Complete half-period inversion minus the proved zero row gives exactly T_ne0=sum_(V<|j|<=2V)sum_(x mod q)(B_j(x)-A_j/q)G_N(x^2-j), with q^(-1)=(4N)^(-1); the constant tail has zero nonzero sampled Fourier coefficients and is the closed zero row. Two-element frequency orbits are 1<=v<H/2 and contribute (Bhat_j(2dv)+Bhat_j(-2dv))K(-v^2,-j;c), with no conjugacy because B_j is complex. The unique nonzero fixed point is v=H/2=N/d and has C_j=Bhat_j(q/2)=sum_x(-1)^xB_j(x). Literal spatial BV gives |C_j|<<M^(-3/4)X^epsilon. With D_j=(-1)^jC_j, sup|D_j|+Var_j(D_j)<<K M^(-3/4)X^epsilon, while opening the fold kernel gives sup_I|sum_(j in I)(-1)^jK(-(N/d)^2,-j;c)|<<c log(2c), because c/2-u is a nonzero unit for every u mod c*. Restoring d sqrt(c)/(Nq) and every odd d yields the target-safe fold bound <<M^(-1/4)X^epsilon. The nearest-cell intervals k^2-k+1<=Nn<=k^2+k partition the positive integers, so the accepted O(VX^epsilon) root count intersects the O(M) physical support to give L_U(V)<<min(M,V)X^epsilon. Hence a genuine signed square-root incidence theorem would be target-sized for every V, but no such theorem is proved. The accepted one-variable BV data do not imply a target mixed rectangular norm because the moving cell has a diagonal atomic trace; ordinary centered completion followed by absolute frequency summation gives only sqrt(N)tau(N)log(2N)^2 and restores N^(1/2)M^(-3/4). These are route-scoped capacities, not impossibility or lower-bound claims. The paired interior nonzero modes remain open.
